formula: Object + is / am / are + V3 + (by + Subject)
auxiliary: is (singular noun, he, she, it), are (plural noun, you, we, they), am (I)
usage: Daily routines, general truths, administrative procedures, aur regular legal notices ke liye. Active ka V1/V_s/es passive mein 'is/am/are + V3' ban jata hai.

patterns.affirmative: The High Court registry publishes the daily cause list every evening.
patterns.negative: The registry does not accept unsigned affidavits.
patterns.interrogative: Does the court clerk maintain the digital case diary?

keyTip: EXAM TRAP: Active ke 'do/does' ko passive mein mat le jayein. Passive mein helping verb strictly 'is/am/are' hoti hai: 'The list is published', not 'The list does published'.

formula: Object + is / am / are + being + V3 + (by + Subject)
auxiliary: is / am / are + being (continuous aspect ke liye 'being' mandatory hai)
usage: Aisi situations ke liye jo bolte waqt progress mein hain. Active ka 'is/am/are + V-ing' passive mein 'is/am/are + being + V3' banta hai.

patterns.affirmative: The judicial committee is reviewing the pending recruitment rules right now.
patterns.negative: The department is not updating the employee records currently.
patterns.interrogative: Are the forensic technicians examining the hard drive?

keyTip: CRITICAL KEYWORD: 'Being' ke bina continuous passive nahi ban sakta. Agar option mein sirf 'are reviewed' hai, toh wo Simple Present ban jayega. Continuous ke liye 'are being reviewed' choose karein.

tense: Present Perfect Passive (Completed Actions with Present Relevance)
formula: Object + has / have + been + V3 + (by + Subject)
auxiliary: has been (singular subject), have been (plural subject / I / we)
usage: Actions jo haal hi mein complete huye hain aur jinka result present mein relevant hai. Active 'has/have + V3' passive mein 'has/have + been + V3' banta hai.

patterns.affirmative: The government has approved the new High Court service cadre.
patterns.negative: The counsel has not submitted the vakalatnama so far.
patterns.interrogative: Has the Chief Justice constituted the special arbitration bench?

keyTip: CONCORD ALERT: Agar active object plural hai (jaise 'rules'), toh active subject chahe singular ho, passive mein plural auxiliary 'have been' lagegi: 'The rules have been approved'.

tense: Simple Past Passive (Definite Completed Past Events)
auxiliary: was (singular noun, I, he, she, it), were (plural noun, you, we, they)
usage: Past ke kisi specific time par poore huye events ya historical milestones ke liye. Active ka V2 passive mein 'was/were + V3' banta hai.

patterns.affirmative: The division bench delivered the landmark judgment yesterday.
patterns.negative: The investigating officer did not seize the forged cheques.
patterns.interrogative: Did the district magistrate issue the prohibitory orders under Section 144?

keyTip: DID ELIMINATION: Active negative 'did not + V1' passive mein 'was not / were not + V3' banta hai. Passive mein 'did' kabhi use nahi hota.

tense: Past Continuous Passive (Ongoing Past Background Actions)
formula: Object + was / were + being + V3 + (by + Subject)
usage: Past ke kisi point par chal rahe continuous actions ke liye. Active 'was/were + V-ing' passive mein 'was/were + being + V3' banta hai.

patterns.affirmative: The stenographer was typing the confidential deposition when the power tripped.
patterns.negative: The clerks were not auditing the treasury accounts yesterday morning.
patterns.interrogative: Were the system assistants testing the server backup during the outage?

keyTip: PAST CONTINUOUS FORMULA: 'was/were + being + V3'. Option mein se 'being' gayab ho toh wo option foran eliminate kar dein.

tense: Past Perfect Passive (Earlier of Two Past Actions)
auxiliary: had been (sabhi singular aur plural subjects ke sath universal hai)
usage: Past ke kisi second action se pehle complete ho chuke earlier action ke liye. Active 'had + V3' passive mein 'had been + V3' banta hai.

patterns.affirmative: The registry had sealed the electronic voting machines before the observers arrived.
patterns.negative: The department had not notified the revised syllabus before the exam date.
patterns.interrogative: Had the magistrate recorded the statement of the victim before the transfer?

keyTip: BENEFIT OF HAD: Past Perfect mein singular/plural ka tension nahi hota; sabhi ke sath 'had been + V3' lagta hai. Bas 'been' lagana mat bhooliye.

formula: Simple Future: will / shall + be + V3 | Future Perfect: will / shall + have + been + V3
auxiliary: will be + V3 (Simple Future); will have been + V3 (Future Perfect)
usage: Future intentions, official announcements, aur deadline-based future completions ke liye.

patterns.affirmative: The committee will announce the typing test schedule next Monday.
patterns.negative: The candidates will not have completed the documentation before noon.
patterns.interrogative: Will the High Court administration conduct the verification online?

timeMarkers: by the end of this month
keyTip: BASE FORM INTEGRITY: Modal ke baad hamesha base form 'be' ya 'have been' lagti hai. 'Will has been' jaisa koi construction English mein exist nahi karta.

formula: Subject + First Auxiliary + NOT + Remaining Auxiliaries + V3
auxiliary: is not V3 | was not V3 | has not been V3 | is not being V3 | will not be V3
usage: Negative sentences mein negation ka slot hamesha FIRST auxiliary verb ke turant baad hota hai.

patterns.affirmative: The administrative clerk has verified the original caste certificate.
patterns.negative: The original caste certificate has not been verified by the administrative clerk.
patterns.interrogative: Has the original caste certificate not been verified by the administrative clerk?

keyTip: NOT PLACEMENT: Multiple helping verbs hone par 'not' hamesha pehli helping verb ke baad lagta hai: 'has NOT been verified' (sahi), 'has been not verified' (galat).

formula: Yes/No: Aux + Object + V3? | Wh-: Wh-word + Aux + Object + V3? | Who: By whom + Aux + Object + V3?
auxiliary: Tense ke hisaab se initial auxiliary inverted rehti hai
usage: Direct questions ko passive mein convert karne ke liye. Question mark aur interrogative inversion maintain rehti hai.

patterns.affirmative: Did the defense counsel cross-examine the eyewitness in the court?
patterns.negative: Why did the committee reject the application of the appellant?
patterns.interrogative: Who drafted this comprehensive administrative circular?

keyTip: WHO TO BY WHOM: 'Who wrote the letter?' ➔ 'By whom was the letter written?'. Dhyaan rahe 'By whom' ke baad pehle auxiliary 'was' aayegi, fir object 'the letter'.

formula: Unknown/Obvious Agent ➔ Omit 'by + agent' | Intransitive Verb (no object) ➔ No Passive Possible
auxiliary: Standard passive auxiliary as per tense
usage: Agar doer 'someone', 'people', 'they', ya obvious authority ('police', 'doctor') ho toh agent ko omit karein. Agar verb intransitive ho (sleep, die, arrive, go) toh passive construct na karein.

patterns.affirmative: Someone has stolen the case documents from the record room.
patterns.negative: The confidential case documents have been stolen (by someone omitted).
patterns.interrogative: The injured witness died in the district hospital (Intransitive: No Passive Possible).

keyTip: EXAM TRAP: Agar question mein intransitive verb di ho ('He arrived yesterday'), toh option mein 'He was arrived' dekhkar tick mat karein. Intransitive ka passive nahi banta.
